Per-peripheral counts are still pending the reference-manual pass -- ingestion against IMX93RM.pdf (5593 pages) is a separate dedicated pass and has not yet run (#380).  `mipi_dsi: 1` and `lcdif: 1` were transcribed ahead of that pass from the pinned Zephyr v4.4.0 device tree (`dts/arm64/nxp/nxp_mimx93_a55.dtsi`, single `mipi_dsi: dsi@4ae10000` node compatible `nxp,mipi-dsi-dwc`, plus the LCDIF display-controller node -- see the next note), so HW_MIPI_DSI and HW_LCDIF report truthfully for the display path.  A key absent from `peripherals` still defaults to zero and must not be inferred from its absence.

Interim counts from the pinned Zephyr v4.4.1 device tree (#380), all listed in `peripherals_unverified` because a device tree is not a silicon inventory: each count is the number of nodes Zephyr describes, so it is a lower bound, not the reference-manual total.  Source `dts/arm64/nxp/nxp_mimx93_a55.dtsi` unless stated.  `i2c: 8` = `lpi2c1`..`lpi2c8` (`nxp,lpi2c`; the same eight are in `dts/arm/nxp/imx/nxp_imx93_m33.dtsi`).  `spi: 8` = `lpspi1`..`lpspi8` (`nxp,lpspi`); `flexspi1: spi@425e0000` (`nxp,imx-flexspi`) is a memory controller and is not counted, it is covered by `external_memory_interfaces`.  `uart: 2` = `lpuart1: serial@44380000`, `lpuart2: serial@44390000` (`nxp,imx-lpuart`).  `i2s: 1` = `sai3: dai@42660000` (`nxp,dai-sai`); `sai3_2: sai@42660000` (`nxp,mcux-i2s`) is a second binding of the same instance at the same address.  `can_fd: 2` = `flexcan1: can@443a0000`, `flexcan2: can@425b0000` (`nxp,flexcan-fd`).  `watchdog: 2` = `wdog3: watchdog@42490000`, `wdog4: watchdog@424a0000` (`nxp,wdog32`).  `timer_tpm: 6` = `tpm1`..`tpm6` (`nxp,tpm-timer`); the `pwm1`..`pwm6` nodes (`nxp,kinetis-tpm`) are PWM bindings of the same six TPM instances at the same addresses.  The key is `timer_tpm`, not `timer_32bit`, on purpose: gen_soc_caps.py falls PWM_COUNT back to `timer_32bit`, and no native PWM leg is claimed for NX9101 here, so ALP_SOC_PWM_COUNT stays 0 while ALP_SOC_TIMER_COUNT reports 6.  `ethernet_1g: 1` = `enet: enet@42890000` (`nxp,enet1g`).  `usb_2: 2` = `usb1: usbd@4c100000`, `usb2: usbd@4c200000` (`nxp,ehci`).  Seen in the device tree but deliberately NOT keyed: `sar_adc1: adc@44530000` (`nxp,sar-adc`, M33 dtsi only) because the `adc_<N>bit` key needs a resolution the device tree does not state; `gpio1`..`gpio4` (`nxp,imx-rgpio`) because the `gpio` key is a pin count and the nodes carry no `ngpios`; `usdhc1`/`usdhc2` (`nxp,imx-usdhc`) and `edma4` because no ALP_SOC_*_COUNT consumes them and `external_memory_interfaces` already describes SD/eMMC.

i.MX 93 has *no GPU* -- that's a deliberate split with i.MX 95.  Display path is LCDIF (1x `nxp,imx-lcdifv3` display-controller@4ae30000 in the same pinned Zephyr dtsi) driving MIPI-DSI (no 2D GPU acceleration).  Both the MIPI-DSI and LCDIF instances are structured as `peripherals` counts (`mipi_dsi: 1`, `lcdif: 1`): gen_soc_caps.py consumes `lcdif` into ALP_SOC_LCDIF_COUNT / ALP_CAP_HW_LCDIF (issue #379), distinct from mipi_dsi. E8 models its parallel display path as `dpi_parallel`, an unrelated interface, so the LCDIF key stays imx-lcdifv3-specific.

Companion silicon on the Alp Lab E1M-i.MX93 SoM (per the vendor datasheet): NXP PCA9451A PMIC; Murata Type 2DL / 2EL / 2KL / 2LL Wi-Fi 6 + BLE 5.x combo (variant TBD); IW610 Wi-Fi 6 module -- confirm which combo ships on which SKU when the user writes the exact HW config.

Reference docs available locally: IMX93HDG.pdf (Hardware Design Guide, 42 p), IMX93RM.pdf (Reference Manual Rev. 6, 5593 p), AN14413.pdf (PCA9451A PMIC application note).  All cross-referenced in the `datasheet.source` field above.

Ethos-U65 host-core pairing is DOCUMENTED ABSENCE, not an unexamined gap: sourced against IMX93RM Rev. 7 (2026-02-10, 5601 p, https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/IMX93RM.pdf), a newer printing than this file's general `datasheet` provenance block above (Rev. 6, 5593 p, 2025-07-01) -- ONLY this note draws on Rev. 7; every other fact in this spec was ingested against Rev. 6 and this note does not re-verify them at the newer revision. Rev. 7 names no host core for the NPU. §2.2 'System memory map used by all initiators' Table 4 lists the NPU Controller (4A90_0000 (NS) / 5A90_0000 (S), 4 KB) among ALL initiators, not one; Table 5 'System memory map (Cortex-M33)' repeats the identical row in the Cortex-M33's OWN memory map too, so the block sits in both, not exclusively in either. §17.2.8 'Interrupt signals' says only 'See Arm's General Interrupt Controller (GIC) documentation for NPU block interrupts' -- the GIC is the Cortex-A55's controller, not the M33's NVIC. Chapter 17 never names a host core, using only Arm's generic Ethos-U wording 'the external host application processor' (§17.2, §17.2.9). This is weaker-in-kind evidence than the Alif E8 HWRM's Table 10-2 per-master A32/M55-HP/M55-HE access matrix (see `paired_core`'s schema description and `_check_soc_npu_pairing`'s docstring in scripts/validate_metadata.py for the full contrast): an all-initiators memory map plus a GIC pointer, not a per-master permission table -- actual masters are TRDC-governed and undocumented here. `npus[0]` above correctly omits `paired_core` on that basis; this note records why, it does not add one. This is a claim about what the reference manual documents, not about what runs today: NXP's own shipped Yocto/Linux driver stack (`nxp-imx/ethos-u-driver-stack-imx`) does run the Ethos-U driver on the Cortex-M33, with Linux on the Cortex-A55 dispatching to it over shared memory and mailbox IRQs -- a separate, sourced, software-stack fact (see `vendors/nxp-imx93/README.md`) that this documentation gap does not contradict.
